messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT / Sev 2 — Increased 5xx from EU region (euc1). metric spike detected on edge-proxy ELBs and elevated 503/504 across serving tier. PagerDuty: @sara is being paged.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty Incident PD-78912 created. Priority: P2. Incident Commander: sara (oncall). Channels: #incidents, #eng-runtime, bridge open.

sara (oncall): seeing ~15% 5xx for EU clients starting ~09:12 UTC. dashboards show ELB backend_conn_reset and increased target unhealthy counts in euc1b. Investigating now.

kai: I can help with routing checks. ran `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai`. results look normal, TTLs consistent. passing initial tcp traceroutes to ELB IPs.

mike: grabbing ELB health: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:...` looks like many targets in euc1 are UNHEALTHY (health code: 504 timeout). backend logs show `connection reset by peer` from nginx upstream.

sara (oncall): noted. Is this just one AZ or multi-AZ?

lee: euc1b shows 60% targets unhealthy, euc1a & euc1c have intermittent 502 spikes. CloudWatch ENI error metrics show higher attach/detach logs in euc1b around time window.

julia: I'm seeing a correlated increase in EBS stall metrics for i-0euc1b-* instances — io.errors and I/O latency up. Could be noisy host causing kernel backpressure.

sara (oncall): hypothesis: euc1b host-level issues causing backend processes to drop connections -> ELB marks unhealthy -> clients hit remaining AZs and overload. Initial mitigation: mark impacted targets out of service, shift traffic away.

ops-bot: Runbook step: "If AZ-level backend instability, create weighted routing shift to reduce weight for region A by 80% and enable failover to euc2." See runbook: https://intra/runbooks/network/az-instability.

kai: I'm going to create a temporary Route53 weighted policy to shift 70% of traffic out of euc1 while we remediate. Will keep 30% for smoke.

mike: before shifting, can we confirm canaries in euc2 are healthy? run smoke against euc2 origin: `curl -I https://api-euc2.redwood.ai/_health` -> 200 OK, latency 45ms. good.

sara (oncall): do it, @kai. make sure to timestamp and note rollback plan. open a PR to infra-configs for audit.

kai: creating change: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://shift-euc1-weighted.json` submitting... change id ZZZ-111. TTL lowered to 30.

ops-bot: Route53 change ZZZ-111 submitted. propagation expected 30s-120s.

lee: after shift, observed client error rate drop from 15% -> 6% in 2m. latency slightly higher for shifted traffic but acceptable.

julia: continuing to gather logs for euc1b instances. opening host ticket with cloud provider for instance-level networking flapping and EBS IO anomalies.

sara (oncall): good. I'll declare incident commander and start customer impact notes. Notifying support to prepare Cx communications: impact window approx 09:12–ongoing. Affected: EU customers hitting api.redwood.ai; degraded responses, elevated retries.

mike: for mitigation 2, we should drain unhealthy targets gracefully. `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0abc...` starting drain for euc1b.

kai: running a gradual traffic ramp to euc2 to avoid thundering herd. monitoring token costs and latency.

pagerduty-bot: Hand-off reminder: @sara to @kai at 09:40 UTC if no longer available. Please ack.

sara (oncall): ack. heading to another meeting in 10. I'll hand commander to @kai unless anything blocks.

kai: I acknowledge, taking IC at 09:40 UTC. overview: runway mitigation is weighted DNS shift + draining euc1b targets + cloud provider ticket for EBS/ENI.

lee: additional detail — kernel logs on euc1b hosts show network interface qdisc drops and repeated ENI detach/attach events. might be noisy hypervisor or underlying network fabric. Provider ticket ID: CLOUD-54321 opened.

julia: also saw increased db connection churn for instances in euc1b around same time; reducing connection pool timeouts on services in euc1 might help short term. pushing config change: `service-configs -> reduce pool.max_idle  -> deploy`.

ops-bot: change put into deployment pipeline: CHANGE-8902 queued with canary in euc2 only.

sara (oncall): customer impact note (draft): "Between 09:12-09:40 UTC we observed elevated 5xx responses for some EU customers due to an AZ-level infrastructure degradation affecting compute and storage in euc1b. We shifted traffic to healthy AZs/region and are investigating root cause with the cloud provider. Mitigations applied to restore service: DNS weighted failover, ELB target draining, connection pool adjustments. No data loss observed; requests may have been delayed or retried." Please add details & escalate if legal/compliance customers affected.

mike: notification to sales & CSMs: pinging #customer-notifications with a short blurb.

kai: Cloud provider reports underlying network flap affecting a subset of hypervisors in euc1b; they are migrating instances off noisy hosts. Expected ETA for stabilization: 60–90 minutes.

lee: monitoring shows euc1b target unhealthy slowly recovering as provider migrates; UNHEALTHY -> INITIAL -> HEALTHY transitions noted for several instances.

julia: recommend keeping weighted shift for at least 30 more minutes after all targets show healthy to avoid re-impact on clients.

sara (oncall): agreed. I'll mark impact as partial for customers in EU and put incident in progress. assigning post-incident actions: retro for runbook gaps, consider automated cross-region failover test.

ops-bot: Incident PD-78912 updated: status -> Mitigated; mitigation actions documented. Severity downgraded to P3 at 10:05 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder — please handoff notes and assign RCA owner within 24h.

kai: taking RCA owner. immediate next steps: collect host kernel dumps from affected instances, collect ELB and Route53 change timelines, corroborate provider maintenance logs. will schedule RCA meeting.

sara (oncall): handing off final notes. thanks all. closing IC shift to @kai. :thumbsup:

mike: final customer impact estimate: ~8% of active EU requests experienced errors during peak window, majority recovered via retries; no persistent data corruption. logging baseline attached.

julia: I'll coordinate with SRE to run a targeted chaos test in staging to validate weighted routing automation and failover runbooks.

kai: closing slack thread summary: 1) cause: provider-side hypervisor/network flap in euc1b -> EBS/ENI issues. 2) mitigation: weighted DNS shift to reduce euc1 traffic, drain unhealthy targets, instance migration by provider. 3) impact: partial EU customer degradation 09:12–~10:05 UTC, error rate peaked ~15%. 4) next: RCA and runbook updates.

inc-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (auto) — PD-78912 transitioned to status: mitigated. Link: https://pagerduty/PD-78912
